status: USER-REPORTED HARDWARE RESULTS; one controlled 30-frame run per variant
units: ms; display values are hexadecimal; mean values truncated by firmware
transcription_limit: Rows 1-25 transcribed after magnification. Lower byte/call totals (26-30) are not used and are left null; V35 source is only 283x377 pixels.
interpretation: The instrumented hybrid run was slower: 693 vs 676 ms mean frame time. Decoding was 444 vs 428 ms (about 64% vs 63% of the total); raw Flash copies were 2 ms, compressed fetch 20 vs 17 ms, cached copies 6 ms, first-use CRC 0 ms and presentation about 83-84 ms. These readings do not identify direct raw copies or CRC as the main cost in this warm start-room workload.
limitations: One run per variant; no statistical repeatability claim.
Added per-read timers and changed code placement affect execution; these times cannot be directly compared with V33/V34 to quantify probe overhead.
V33/V34 showed a modest hybrid advantage, but it did not repeat under the added instrumentation; a general hybrid speedup is unproven.
Inclusive asset, simulation and render times overlap with decode/fetch/copy buckets; do not sum all rows.
Millisecond rounding on many short copy operations may accumulate error; zero CRC means no measured whole-millisecond contribution, not disabled verification.
FNV-1a matching is evidence of matching output, not cryptographic proof.
Measured no-input one-tic-per-frame start room; not a guarantee for normal play, movement or firing.
Rows 26-30 are untranscribed and no conclusions depend on their values.
decision: Retain V30 as the gameplay baseline. Next prioritize aggregate per-page decode time/frequency to select codec changes or cache residency based on measured hot pages, without sacrificing raw donor pages blindly.
